messages:
sre-oncall: Kicking off performance burn-in for the glasgow-edge cluster (gpu-a10g-8 pool). Scope: throughput/latency baselining, NVLink health, driver/kernel sanity, and network MTU checks. Follow runbook: https://redwood/infra/runbooks/glasgow-edge-burnin

maria: Thanks. Quick checklist before we start: driver version, kernel, nvidia-smi per node, dmesg for driver OOMs, ethtool MTU/TSO/GSO, and a simple benchmark (batch sweep + p95/throughput). Post outputs inline.

ashwin: Running the basic checks on node g-a10g-003 now:
```
$ uname -r
5.15.0-112-generic
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv,noheader
A10G, 535.86, 24576 MiB
$ modinfo nvidia | grep version
version:        535.86
$ ethtool -S eth0 | head -n3
NIC stats: ...
MTU: 1500
$ dmesg | tail -n50 | grep -i nvrm
(no OOMs)
```
Throughput quick-run (local client -> node):
```
$ python benchmarks/run_inference.py --model /models/llm-7b --batch 4 --seq-len 512 --workers 8
tokens/sec: 18500
latency p50: 22ms p95: 145ms p99: 270ms
```
Observations: baseline ok but p95 is spiky on this node. Capturing full perf trace to s3://redwood-perf/glasgow/1954321000/

jonah: Saw a similar spike on g-a10g-007 earlier. Quick NVLink check shows one node with NVLINK link state DOWN between GPU3<->GPU4. Command:
```
nvlink --status
GPU0-GPU1: OK
GPU1-GPU2: OK
GPU3-GPU4: DOWN
```
Workaround: cycle nvidia-persistenced + restart MIG/SM config. Also check kernel dmesg for ECC or PCI errors.

maria: Good catch. If NVLink is down, some allreduce/kvcache placement will fallback to PCIe causing p95 jumps. Can you run: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo nvidia-smi topo -m` and paste the output? Also, what is MTU on the host? If it's 1500 vs 9000 we see extra CPU overhead for RPCs.

ashwin: After restart on g-a10g-007:
```
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo nvidia-smi topo -m
Topology:
GPU0  GPU1  GPU2  GPU3  GPU4
...
GPU3-GPU4: NVLINK
```
Re-ran benchmark (same params) with kv-cache enabled: tokens/sec: 26800, p50: 18ms p95: 82ms p99: 160ms
So NVLink fix + kv-cache yields big improvement.

jonah: Also noticed kernel offload settings were disabled on one node (g-a10g-005 had GRO/TSO off). Quick fix: `ethtool -K eth0 tso on gso on gro on` — after that the network CPU overhead dropped and p95 improved ~10-15%.

maria: Notes for handoff: we need a short artifact set per node: - nvidia-smi summary - dmesg grep nvrm/pci - ethtool -k/mtu - benchmark results for batch sweep [1,2,4,8,16] and seq-len [128,512,2048] - any NVLink anomalies captured
Acceptance criteria (provisional): p95 <= 120ms at batch=8 seq=512 across 90% of nodes in pool; no driver OOMs or ECC errors during 2h soak; NVLink fabric OK on GPUs that should have NVLINK.

deploy-bot: Canary run completed for the platform agent on glasgow-edge, no agent errors reported.

ashwin: Did a quick batch sweep summary (aggregated across 12 nodes):
- batch 1 seq512: p95 median 210ms
- batch 4 seq512: p95 median 130ms
- batch 8 seq512: p95 median 95ms (95th percentile nodes hit 140ms due to one NVLink flake)
- batch 16 seq512: p95 median 120ms, but memory pressure + OOM risk on smallest GPU configs
Throughput tokens/sec improves predictably, but cost per token increases beyond batch 8 due to memory-driven slowdowns.

maria: Action items:
- ashwin: collect per-node artifacts into s3://redwood-perf/glasgow/1954321000/ and attach checksums (today EOD)
- jonah: add NVLink health check to provisioning scripts and mark nodes with inconsistent topo as quarantine (ticket infra-glasgow-137)
- ops: validate MTU and offload settings as part of the image build (use mtu=9000 where supported)

jonah: I'll open infra-glasgow-137 and include the NVLink diagnostic script + remediation steps. If we see repeat flakes, plan is to reprovision NIC firmware and escalate to vendor.

maria: Once artifacts are in S3, I'll create the handoff doc for eng-platform with the acceptance criteria above. If everyone is happy with the thresholds, we can cut the initial capacity ramp to 60% and monitor cost/latency for 24 hrs.

sre-oncall: Sounds good. For the audit trail please ensure each node's benchmark CSV and the `dmesg` excerpt are included. After 24h soak, we'll re-run the full suite and close the runbook. :thumbsup:

ashwin: Uploading artifacts now, ping me if anything missing.

maria: Passing to eng-platform for rollout when artifacts and infra ticket are ready. :white_check_mark:
